final_message:
The draft September 2026 write-up for Bluebird Bakery is ready for the reviewer. The script ran without errors, and I wrote 8 commentary bullets into section 1 of the report. The "DRAFT" banner is still in place.

**Data quality: 1 mismatch, which the reviewer needs to settle.** In Mar 2026, "Total for Professional Services" says **2,225.00**, but the lines under it add up to **2,200.00** (a 25.00 difference). The analysis uses the line-level figures; I didn't decide which number is right. There are also two places where the script had to work out the sheet's structure itself:
- "Total Delivery" had no heading row, so the script grouped the two lines above it, which add up to it in every month.
- "Charitable Donations" had no values and no total row, so the 4 rows after it weren't grouped under it.

Year-over-year and trailing-twelve-month figures aren't available because the export only covers 9 months (Jan–Sep 2026).

**Main points:**
- **Revenue was 81,300**, up 17.7% on August (69,050) and 17.3% above the prior 6-month average. That includes **12,000 from "Wholesale Accounts"**, a new stream that was zero in the previous 6 months.
- **Gross margin was 65.3%**, up from 59.6% in August and the highest month in the export.
- **Operating expenses rose 21.0% to 31,570**, almost all from Wages & Salaries (16,000 → 21,000). Payroll had been flat at 17,600 a month from April to August. The commentary asks the reviewer whether this is a one-off or a new level.
- **Net income was 21,553**, up from 15,077, and positive in all 9 months. Meanwhile **cash fell to 37,600**, down 10,800 over six months, and equity also fell. I worded this as a question for the reviewer (for example, owner draws) rather than giving a cause.

**Accounts that fell into "Other Opex":** Instagram Ads, Mystery Shopper Program and Supplier Rebates.

The report's movers table shows Mystery Shopper Program as "from 0", but it isn't new: it has been 400 every quarter (Mar, Jun and Sep). The commentary says so.
